top_news.title: Model-agnostic PII detection with LLMs
top_news.dek: AWS introduced a model-agnostic PII detection framework for Amazon Bedrock that uses prompt-based instructions instead of retraining.
top_news.brief: This approach allows developers to detect PII by defining entity types in prompts rather than code. It avoids the risks of training models on uncleaned data, which can lead to memorization and accidental leakage of sensitive information. The framework has been benchmarked against nine LLM-based detectors across five public corpora.

top_news.brief: InquiryIQ integrates with Clearview's facial recognition database to automatically surface social media accounts, personal associates, and other online activity. The tool reportedly utilizes models from xAI to process and synthesize information about individuals identified through the platform.

primary.title: StochBench: A Domain-Specific Benchmark for Stochastic Processes in Lean
primary.summary: Leading benchmarks for formal theorem proving with large language models are small collections drawn from competition math, such as the IMO and Putnam, that poorly represent field-specific applications. We introduce StochBench, a Lean 4 benchmark of 450 graduate stochastic-processes problems at varying abstraction levels, each paired with its natural-language source. Addressing a field underrepresented in Mathlib, it covers finite and countable Markov chains, renewal processes, random walks, martingales, stopping times, queues, Brownian motion, stochastic calculus, weak convergence, and Poisso

primary.title: Model-agnostic PII detection with LLMs
primary.summary: A configurable, model-agnostic detector that turns any large language model on Amazon Bedrock into a PII detector. Because the entities to detect live in a prompt rather than in code, one detector adapts to new entity types without retraining, and it outperforms an off-the-shelf tool across five public corpora and nine LLM-based detectors.

primary.title: Agent Evaluation Metric for multi-turn conversations
primary.summary: Multi-turn agents fail in ways single-turn evaluation misses: one early mistake corrupts every later turn. This post introduces the Agent Evaluation Metric (AEM), a decomposable, turn-level way to measure agent quality, applied to its first dimension, correctness, to pinpoint the turn that caused a failure and separate it from the turns that inherited it.
